correctness.rationale: The exact signed-permutation polyhedron has 24 vertices, 36 edges and 14 supporting facets; 36 edge sign crossings, constant on each of five exhaustive connected normal chambers, yield the section counts 8,10,6,8,6. Three analytically evaluated spherical solid angles with total chamber area pi/12 produce a positive, normalized three-atom probability law. Exact rational sign and edge-intersection checks, independent Jacobian quadrature and 180000 sampled normals corroborate but do not replace the proof. Non-generic direction sets have Haar measure zero.

originality.rationale: The complete central-section vertex-count law for the Kelvin truncated octahedron is neither an angle distribution, an affine-section area distribution nor an exact law for another polyhedron. Direct comparisons were made to Socha (1988) and Ferraro–Zaninetti (2011) full texts, to relevant 1981 and 1995 abstracts, and to related published geometric laws. A material risk remains from inaccessible 1981 full text; historical uniqueness is not certified.

value.rationale: A complete exact section-type classification for a canonical space-filling Archimedean/BCC Voronoi polyhedron gives three nontrivial probabilities and an explicit five-chamber normal-fan mechanism; this natural discrete invariant is not determined by published area/angle distributions or by formulas for unrelated solids. It is a useful exact benchmark for geometric probability and stereology, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
